title: Release baseline consolidation
objective: Consolidate only reviewed release-critical changes onto the dense QQ release authority and publish a validated release candidate source branch without tagging or publishing artifacts

oracles: Existing portable, strict-Python, native compiler, and release policy suites

handoff.summary: Consolidated the reviewed dense-QQ release authority with the two GCC 13 arbitrary-prime polynomial fixes and the Windows clang-cl reproducible path-map fix. Reconciled stale machine-readable task authority: only already-integrated implementation lanes were closed, historical cross-lane shared claims were returned to integration ownership, one precise JavaScript-backend reproducibility claim was admitted, and the all-contract gate now passes 187 contracts without suppressing overlap detection. A live Windows x64 clang-cl witness accepted the three forwarded prefix maps and observed the logical __FILE__ path. The focused polynomial resource witness and complete FFI suite pass. Required architecture, portable, and strict-Python gates pass at ff05b2b7bf203ead711c3601a805907804a0133f after an ordinary build populated this fresh worktree's generated runtime caches.
risks: The first portable receipt failed only because the no-install worktree had compiler/native cache artifacts but not the ordinary symbolic backend and module/runtime cache manifests; pnpm build populated those expected generated assets and the unchanged candidate then passed all 387 portable tests.

macOS ZeroMQ source rebuilding, release-license remediation, Linux ARM baseline authority, baseline-to-SEA assembly, startup instrumentation, and the unfinished compiler-core prologue are intentionally excluded and require their own reviewed integration.
next_steps: Use ff05b2b7bf203ead711c3601a805907804a0133f as the common source authority for current Linux x64, Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64 platform validation.
Layer independently approved distribution fixes in follow-up integration commits without rewriting this baseline evidence.
